chapter: Family, the reunion retold and sound effects
title: Whistles and radio sound-effect devices
summary: Morehouse demonstrates his pitchpipe, Latin percussion toys, the Rinso White whistle, a baby cry and a ship's foghorn from his days as an NBC sound man.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: Hmmm. Great. What is that Chauncey? It's a round metal thing. What do you use it for?
Well this is supposed to give you an A, an F or an E. (BLOWS INTO DEVICE)
Yeah, that's an E. This is called a pitchpipe.
Ah thank you. What we have here is a number of whistles and percussion instruments. Okay. What is that? (SOUND OF CLACKING) Do you use that along with the drums?
Good, okay. Remember that little balance? (SOUND OF RINGING)
Okay. You use that as Egyptian bells.
Okay. Do you remember this little whistle? What is that? What do you call that?
It's called a Rinso White whistle.
Chauncey was sound man for NBC.
And he did the Rinso White whistle?
I see. That's a little wooden whistle with a plunger that goes in and out in the back.
That's for the Rinso White commercial.
Does that mean anything? That's another, it looks like a whistle of some sort. Do you know what they use that for?
Okay, let me see what else you have here,- continue on 2-35B
Yes, he did. I think that's a duck call.
I think it is. (SOUND OF WHISTLE) No, this is a baby crying. Now make the baby cry, honey.
You did sound effects on radio.
That was supposed to be a baby crying on radio?
Okay. That whistle is called a baby crying in this thing, isn't it?
When you were doing sound effects on radio, one of the devices you used was this block of wood that you blew into.
In a fog, right. A foghorn, yes a foghorn. (MR. MOREHOUSE REPEATS SOUND EFFECT) That's very good.
